artifacts.summary: Verifies the warn.sorry double-count root cause (line 144 \bsorry\b regex crossing the '.' boundary), independently confirms the (?<![.\w])sorry\b fix against 5 discriminating cases including the same-line non-regression case, traces the real sorry_count==0 downstream gate in lean-implementation-agent.md and cslib-implementation-agent.md, and specifies a new toolchain-free regression fixture under a new agent-system/extensions/lean/scripts/tests/ directory.

memory_candidates.content: In Python regex, \b (word boundary) fires at any transition between a \w char and a non-\w char, including '.'. So \bsorry\b matches the 'sorry' inside 'warn.sorry' or any 'foo.sorry' dotted-qualified name -- not just standalone 'sorry' tokens. Fix: use a negative lookbehind excluding '.' and word chars, e.g. (?<![.\w])sorry\b, to require the match not be preceded by a dot or another word character. This generalizes to any 'exclude dotted-qualifier false positives from \b<word>\b scans' scenario.

agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/ establishes a repo-wide shell-test convention: set -uo pipefail; pass()/fail()/info() helpers with PASSED/FAILED integer counters; mktemp -d workdir with trap ... EXIT cleanup; synthetic-only fixtures built via heredocs (never touches the real repo tree); exit 0 on all-pass, 1 on any-fail. test-census-count.sh additionally documents an 'anti-vacuous-test guard': every bug-class fixture must assert both the naive/wrong number and the corrected number on the same fixture, so a fixture only a broken implementation would fail is required. Non-core extensions (e.g. lean) currently lack their own scripts/tests/ subdirectory -- new extension-level regression tests should follow this same convention in a new <extension>/scripts/tests/ dir.

lean-sorry-census.sh's sorry_count output is a hard implementation-completion gate, not just an informational metric: both lean-implementation-agent.md and cslib-implementation-agent.md require sorry_count == 0 before marking a task implemented, and cslib's pr-description-format.md requires the literal 'sorry_count: 0' string in PR descriptions. Any counting bug in this script (e.g. phantom matches) can therefore falsely block legitimate completions, not merely misreport a number -- worth checking downstream consumers' gating logic whenever auditing a shared census/count script.
